delete.summary: Reset my email signature to the default: remove yours, our signature is used again
delete.description: Remove your email signature for a brand: new threads end with our default signature again. Idempotent. Every email we send for a brand ends with a signature. By default it is ours: the sending mailbox's name, then `Distribute.you | Marketing Agency` (`signature: null`). Set your own and it replaces ours on every NEW email thread of the brand: the email itself (a cold email, or an email you pushed through the API with the `email_pushed_via_api` trigger), every follow-up, and every reply we send in that thread, AI replies included. A thread keeps the signature it started with: changing or resetting yours applies to new threads only, so a conversation never switches signature halfway. A brand that is not one of the authenticated org's brands is a 404 `brand_not_in_org`. Pass-through to instantly-service /orgs/email-signature; upstream errors are forwarded field-for-field. Declares no cost.

schema.description: The brand (uuid) the signature is for

post.summary: Stop the queued follow-ups of named leads a campaign emailed in error
post.description:
Pass-through to instantly-service POST /orgs/followup-cuts. For leads a campaign should never have written to (a sourcing mistake): the rest of their sequence will not go out. Every other lead of the campaign keeps its follow-ups. Body `{ campaignId, leadEmails[], reason }`. Not an opt-out: nothing is recorded as unsubscribe or suppression. All or nothing on names: an email the campaign never wrote to is a 404 `leads_not_in_campaign` and nothing is cut. Idempotent (`already_cut`). Audited: who, when, why (GET /v1/followup-cuts). A lead that could not be cut answers 502.

Request body: documented from instantly-service POST /orgs/followup-cuts, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

campaignId.description: The campaign (campaign-service id) that emailed these leads

leadEmails.description: The leads of that campaign whose queued follow-ups stop. Every other lead keeps its follow-ups.

reason.description: Why: stored on the audit row

example.reason: Sourcing bug handed this campaign people it was not meant to write to

200.description: Per-lead outcome as returned by instantly-service

get.summary: When we may email one lead (weekdays, local hours, timezone)
get.description: Pass-through to instantly-service GET /orgs/sending-schedule. Returns the weekdays and the local start/end hour we may email this lead in, the lead's timezone (`timezoneIsDefault` when we hold no zone for them) and whether a sequence exists. Never a 404: a lead this org holds nothing for reads as the default schedule. The org boundary is the authenticated org. `brand_id` is also forwarded as the `x-brand-id` identity header. The whole query string is forwarded verbatim — the parameters listed here are the ones documented today, not a whitelist. Upstream error bodies are forwarded field-for-field. Declares no cost — it sends nothing.

post.summary: Charge a stated amount against the org's saved card
post.description: Charges `amountCents` against the card the calling org already saved, off-session — no redirect and no hosted page, so a customer paying for several things one at a time stays on the page after the first (hosted) payment saved the card. The org charged is the authenticated one (resolved from the Bearer key); no orgId is accepted in the body. Transparent proxy to billing-service POST /internal/accounts/by-org/{orgId}/charge — request body and response are owned by billing-service (passthrough). Every refusal carries a stable `code` and reaches the caller field-for-field under billing's own status (CLAUDE.md #7): 402 `charge_declined`, 409 `no_chargeable_payment_method`, 409 `card_not_chargeable_off_session`, 429 `charge_backoff`, 502 `upstream_error`. The gateway adds no retry or backoff of its own.

get.description: List all generated emails across campaigns for a brand: the lead each was written for and the subject and body of every step. Returns the same shape as GET /campaigns/{id}/emails. Proxies to content-generation-service GET /generations. The query string is forwarded verbatim, so every filter content-generation-service accepts can be asked for; the parameters below are the ones it documents today, not a whitelist this gateway enforces. brandId is the one this gateway itself requires.

parameters.name: x-request-id
parameters.description: Correlation id for this request. Echoed back verbatim in the `x-request-id` response header. Omit it and the gateway generates a UUID, so the response header is always present. Useful for tying a response back to the call that produced it when issuing concurrent requests.

parameters.name: x-org-id
parameters.description: With a user key (`distrib.usr_*`): the organization this request acts in, one of the key user's organizations (GET /v1/me lists them). Same as the `orgId` query parameter. Needed only when the user belongs to several organizations and the request names no brand; otherwise optional.

parameters.name: x-user-id
parameters.description: External user ID (e.g. Clerk user ID `user_2abc...`). Required when using an app key (`distrib.app_*`) on endpoints that need user context. Ignored when using a user key (`distrib.usr_*`).

parameters.name: x-campaign-id
parameters.description: Campaign ID. Automatically injected by workflow-service on workflow HTTP calls. Optional — forwarded to downstream services for tracking.

parameters.name: x-brand-id
parameters.description: Brand ID(s), comma-separated UUIDs. Supports multi-brand campaigns. Forwarded to downstream services. With a user key it also selects the organization the request acts in: the one of the user's organizations holding every named brand (same for `brandId` in the query or a JSON body).

parameters.name: x-workflow-slug
parameters.description: Workflow slug. Automatically injected by workflow-service on workflow HTTP calls. Optional — forwarded to downstream services for tracking.

parameters.name: x-feature-slug
parameters.description: Feature slug. Optional — forwarded to downstream services and runs for tracking.

The undo of POST /v1/emails/manual-qualifications, for a person who picked the wrong kind by mistake. After the withdrawal the lead reads as it did before anybody said anything: no standing human statement, and the automatic classification takes over again. The body is forwarded byte-identical and this gateway never enumerates the reply-kind vocabulary; instantly-service owns it. Transparent proxy to email-gateway → instantly-service; the response shape is owned upstream.

post.summary: Record that a person asked a human to stop contacting them
post.description:
A prospect rarely clicks the unsubscribe link: they send an SMS, they call, they reply to a thread somebody forwarded them, they say it in person. This records that statement — it is never inferred — and instantly-service then honours it: the sending stops and the person reads as unsubscribed on the delivery status. Scope is the PERSON, not a campaign, and the row is a consent record: who stated it, when, and through which channel. Re-recording a standing opt-out is idempotent. The body is forwarded byte-identical and this gateway never enumerates the channel vocabulary; instantly-service owns it, so a value it rejects comes back as its own refusal rather than a local 400. Transparent proxy to email-gateway → instantly-service; the response shape is owned upstream.

Request body: documented from email-gateway-service POST /orgs/opt-outs, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

Values it rejects are round-tripped from upstream, not refused here.

post.summary: Generate a journalist-quote pitch
post.description:
Proxy to content-generation-service POST /generate-expert-quote-pitch. Generates a Featured.com-compliant pitch (100-2500 char constraint) for an expert journalist quote opportunity. Body + response shapes are owned by the downstream service.

Request body: documented from content-generation-service POST /generate-expert-quote-pitch, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

variables.description: Variable values to substitute into the stored 'expert-quote-pitch' template. ALL of the template's declared variables are REQUIRED and must be non-empty (missing/empty → 400). For the platform template the required set is three generic-JSON blobs: `expert` (the person whose quote gets published — name/title/bio/photo/linkedin/answer context), `brands` (the brand(s) the expert represents — multibrand, usually an array), and `journalistRequest` (the journalist's request). Inner JSON shape per variable is caller's choice; the authoritative input list is published via GET /platform-prompts?type=expert-quote-pitch (.variables).

templateType.description: Explicit prompt type to render, overriding feature assignment + platform default. Resolution order: templateType ▸ feature assignment for featureSlug ▸ platform default 'expert-quote-pitch'.

model.description: LLM model to generate with (version-free alias). Provider is derived automatically: anthropic → haiku | sonnet | opus; google → flash-lite | flash | flash-pro | pro; deepseek → deepseek-flash (DeepSeek V4 Flash) | deepseek-pro (DeepSeek V4 Pro); zai → glm-flash (glm-4.7-flashx) | glm-pro (glm-5.2); moonshot → kimi-flash (kimi-k2.6) | kimi-pro (kimi-k3). The six deepseek/zai/moonshot aliases are called directly on each vendor's OpenAI-compatible API. That path is text-only, which this service never exceeds; note that JSON-mode enforcement there is best-effort (fails loud rather than degrading), and a vendor whose account is out of credit answers 429 — surfaced as an error naming the provider, never silently rerouted to another vendor. Omit to use the default 'pro' (google) — unchanged from before this field existed.

post.summary: Write one cold email for a brand and a sample recipient

Proxy to content-generation-service POST /preview-email. Writes the first email of the sequence the product would send, for a brand of the calling org and a sample recipient, before any campaign exists. companyDomain.description: The recipient's company website or domain.

headline.description: The recipient's own one-line professional headline.

audience.description: The audience / segment the sample recipient was found in, in plain English. Given to the model as context.

offerId.description: Which offer of the brand to pitch. Required by brand-service only when the brand sells several offers.

post.summary: Get ready to write preview emails for a brand (fire and forget)
post.description:
Proxy to content-generation-service POST /preview-email/prepare. Starts, in the background, the brand read POST /v1/content/preview-email will need for this brand, so the first preview only waits for the model. Answers 202 at once with the downstream body and status forwarded as-is; idempotent per org + brand. The brand read is billed to the calling org. Body + response shapes are owned by the downstream service (today: body { brandId, offerId? }, response { brandId, status }).

Request body: documented from content-generation-service POST /preview-email/prepare, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

parameters.description: Filter by status (defaults to 'active')
parameters.name: status
x-request-id
parameters.description: Correlation id for this request. Echoed back verbatim in the `x-request-id` response header. Omit it and the gateway generates a UUID, so the response header is always present. Useful for tying a response back to the call that produced it when issuing concurrent requests.

parameters.name: x-org-id
parameters.description: With a user key (`distrib.usr_*`): the organization this request acts in, one of the key user's organizations (GET /v1/me lists them). Same as the `orgId` query parameter. Needed only when the user belongs to several organizations and the request names no brand; otherwise optional.

parameters.name: x-user-id
parameters.description: External user ID (e.g. Clerk user ID `user_2abc...`). Required when using an app key (`distrib.app_*`) on endpoints that need user context. Ignored when using a user key (`distrib.usr_*`).

parameters.name: x-campaign-id
parameters.description: Campaign ID. Automatically injected by workflow-service on workflow HTTP calls. Optional — forwarded to downstream services for tracking.

parameters.name: x-brand-id
parameters.description: Brand ID(s), comma-separated UUIDs. Supports multi-brand campaigns. Forwarded to downstream services. With a user key it also selects the organization the request acts in: the one of the user's organizations holding every named brand (same for `brandId` in the query or a JSON body).

parameters.name: x-workflow-slug
parameters.description: Workflow slug. Automatically injected by workflow-service on workflow HTTP calls. Optional — forwarded to downstream services for tracking.

parameters.name: x-feature-slug
parameters.description: Feature slug. Optional — forwarded to downstream services and runs for tracking.

parameters.name: x-request-id

parameters.name: x-org-id
parameters.description: With a user key (`distrib.usr_*`): the organization this request acts in, one of the key user's organizations (GET /v1/me lists them). Same as the `orgId` query parameter. Needed only when the user belongs to several organizations and the request names no brand; otherwise optional.

parameters.name: x-user-id
parameters.description: External user ID (e.g. Clerk user ID `user_2abc...`). Required when using an app key (`distrib.app_*`) on endpoints that need user context. Ignored when using a user key (`distrib.usr_*`).

parameters.name: x-campaign-id
parameters.description: Campaign ID. Automatically injected by workflow-service on workflow HTTP calls. Optional — forwarded to downstream services for tracking.

parameters.name: x-brand-id

parameters.description: Feature slug. Optional — forwarded to downstream services and runs for tracking.

post.summary: Ingest a conversion event (no Clerk auth — per-brand token)
post.description:
PUBLIC conversion-tracking ingest. Called directly by third-party client websites (conversion snippet / server-side postback). NOT authenticated by a Clerk session — the per-brand publishable token travels in the `x-conversion-token` header (or `Authorization: Bearer`) and is verified downstream. Proxied to lead-service POST /public/conversions; the raw JSON body is forwarded untouched. Response (expected 200 { received: true }, or its 400/401) is owned by the downstream service.

Request body: documented from lead-service POST /public/conversions, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

event.description: The conversion that happened on the client's website. "sale" is the terminal "a customer paid" signal (carries a revenue value in valueCents). The legacy spelling "purchase" is still accepted and normalized to "sale" so already-configured integrations keep firing. The special value "ping" is a liveness heartbeat the on-page tag fires on page-load — it is NOT a conversion (no attribution, not counted, excluded from eventTypesSeen), it only proves the tag is alive.

dedupeKey.description: Client-supplied idempotency key. When present, uniqueness is per (brand, dedupeKey). When absent, dedupe is per (brand, event, email-or-phone, calendar-day).

valueCents.description: Optional conversion value in cents — the revenue attached to the event (primarily the "sale" terminal signal).

schema.description: A conversion event reported by a client's website pixel.

post.summary: Claim an invite code for the authenticated org
post.description:
Pass-through to client-service POST /internal/invites/claim. Send only { code }: the gateway supplies the downstream-required inviteeOrgId from the authenticated identity, and discards any inviteeOrgId in the request body so a caller can never claim on behalf of another org. Downstream orchestrates: record claim row -> grant credits to inviter + invitee via billing-service -> send the invite confirmation emails via transactional-email-service. post.summary: Create a buying-signal audience
post.description:
Proxy to human-service POST /orgs/audiences/signal. Creates an audience of people showing a buying signal (first type: linkedin_engagement, people who engaged with competitor LinkedIn posts). Body { brandId, offerId?, name?, nlPrompt, status?, signal: { type, windowDays, competitorPages? } }; the body's brandId is also forwarded as the x-brand-id identity header. Request + response shapes are owned by human-service. Downstream status and body (400, 409 name conflict, the signal provider's named 4xx such as a malformed competitor page) are forwarded verbatim.

Request body: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/signal, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

offerId.description: The brand-service offer this audience belongs to. Stored verbatim, like brandId. Omitted = brand-wide.

name.description: Audience name (English), unique per (brand, offer). Omitted = apollo-service's label (competitor slugs + window).

nlPrompt.description: Who among the engagers is worth writing to, in plain English (people, not only companies). Stored as the audience target: the pre-pay screen judges every engager teaser (name, title, headline, employer) against it before any email is paid for.

windowDays.description: Age of the competitor posts whose engagers are served, in days, counted back from each serve (rolling).

competitorPages.description: 1-3 competitor LinkedIn company page URLs (https://www.linkedin.com/company/<slug>/). Validated by apollo-service, whose named 400 is relayed.

filters.description: Apollo base filters. Must be empty: apollo-service refuses Apollo filters beside this signal with a named 400 (relayed), since its people are LinkedIn engagers, not an Apollo search. Omitted = {}.

201.description: Created audience (human-service { audience })

post.summary: Build the active audience portfolio of a brand + offer from its ICP
post.description:
Proxy to human-service POST /orgs/audiences/portfolio. Derives the active audiences (cold split audiences + buying-signal audiences) for a brand + offer from the ICP text the customer validated. Answers once the cold audiences exist (seconds) with status "building"; the buying-signal audiences finish in the background and flip it to "ready". Poll the same POST until ready: a replay of the same brand + offer returns the current set without re-spending. The gateway waits up to 10 minutes upstream. Request + response shapes are owned by human-service; downstream status and body (400, 409, 502) are forwarded verbatim.

Request body: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences/portfolio, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

targetAudience.description: The ICP text the customer validated (who they sell to), in their words. Every portfolio audience is derived from it, and every one carries the same person-level restatement of it as its nlPrompt (the target the pre-pay screen judges each teaser against).

post.summary: Create an audience
post.description:
Proxy to human-service POST /orgs/audiences. Request + response shapes owned by human-service. Forwarded untransformed.

Request body: documented from human-service POST /orgs/audiences, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

provider.description: The provider this audience commits to. apollo/apify when persisting a candidate from /suggest; crm for a brand whose audience is its uploaded contact list (served by crm-service — no filters/apolloAudienceId, brand-scoped). Omit for a neutral audience.

apolloAudienceId.description: Pointer to the faithful Apollo audience owned by apollo-service, when persisting an apollo candidate. Omit for a neutral / apify audience.

crmUploadId.description: Bind this audience to ONE imported CRM source (a crm-service upload id of the same brand). Every CRM serve made under this audience is then restricted to the people of that file, so several bound audiences can coexist for one brand and each is independently pausable + independently costed. Validated against the brand's uploads at creation (400 if it is not one of them). Omit to keep the whole-brand behaviour. Immutable afterwards.

signedUp.description: true = only people who signed up to the brand's product (a signup on its auth provider); false = only people who did not.

replied.description: false = only people who NEVER wrote to the brand on any conversation channel (email, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, an answer to our outreach); true = only people who did.

reachableBy.description: Only people holding a phone / an email. A phone channel (WhatsApp, SMS) wants 'phone': a person served without one is burned for nothing.

segment.description: A part of the brand's own CRM, as crm-service's PeopleSegment states it (passed through verbatim, validated by crm-service): dealStages [{stage, pipeline?}], dealStatuses, tags, reached / notReached (funnel steps), includeClients, includeOptedOut. Lists OR, keys AND; clients and opted-out people are out unless stated. Names come from crm-service GET /orgs/contacts/segments.

crmPeople.description: Bind this CRM audience to the brand's merged PEOPLE matching a filter (e.g. {signedUp: true, replied: false} = product signups who never answered) instead of to an imported file, optionally scoped to a `segment` of the brand's own CRM (e.g. {segment: {dealStages: [{pipeline: 'Sales Pipeline', stage: 'Form Filled - No Appointment'}]}}). Requires provider 'crm'; exclusive with crmUploadId. A segment crm-service refuses is a 400 carrying its reason. Every serve passes the filter to crm-service (same brand-wide no-re-serve forever); each served person carries its phone when crm-service holds one. Validated against crm-service's serve-stats at creation (its counts become the audience's Size / Remaining). Immutable afterwards.

offerId.description: The offer this audience belongs to — a brand-service offer id. Scopes the audience to one distinct thing the brand sells; name uniqueness becomes per (org, brand, offer), so two offers of the same brand may each own an audience with the same name. Stored as-is: human-service defines no offer semantics and does not resolve the id (same as brandId). Omit to keep the brand-wide behaviour. Immutable afterwards.

apolloCount.description: Optional count snapshot the caller already obtained from /orgs/people/search/dry-run (apollo). Stored as-is; refresh-count re-computes it server-side later. Accepts null (e.g. an apify-source candidate carries apolloCount: null).

apifyCount.description: Optional apify count snapshot (see apolloCount). Accepts null (e.g. an apollo-source candidate carries apifyCount: null).

get.description: Proxy to crm-service GET /orgs/contacts/segments. post.summary: Serve the next batch of un-served contacts for a brand
post.description:
Proxy to crm-service POST /orgs/contacts/serve-next. Request body forwarded verbatim — crm-service owns its shape. Response shape owned by crm-service.

Request body: documented from crm-service POST /orgs/contacts/serve-next, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

limit.description: Max contacts to serve this call. Defaults to 100.

uploadIds.description: Restrict the serve to these imported CRM files (ids from GET /orgs/contacts/uploads). Omit for the whole brand. Suppression stays brand-wide: a contact already served through another file is never returned again, whichever file is used.

signedUp.description: true = only people who signed up to the brand's product (its auth provider, e.g. Clerk); false = only people who did not.

replied.description: false = only people who NEVER wrote to the brand on any conversation channel (Gmail / WhatsApp / LinkedIn inbound, any answer to our cold email): never written to, or written to without an answer. true = only people who answered. Copilot / API use is the product being used, not a conversation.

reachableBy.description: Only people holding a phone / an email (a list = all).

dealStages.description: CRM pipeline stage: the person has a deal CURRENTLY at one of these stages (the customer's own stage name, optionally its pipeline name; trimmed, case-insensitive). Names come from GET /orgs/contacts/segments.

dealStatuses.description: The deal's CRM status, verbatim (GoHighLevel: open, won, lost, abandoned). With dealStages, the SAME deal must match both.

tags.description: The person's CRM contact carries one of these tags (case-insensitive).

reached.description: The person reached one of these funnel steps, any source the brand connected (form submitted, appointment booked / showed / no-show, signup, website visit, sale).

notReached.description: The person reached none of these steps.

includeClients.description: Default false: people who reached `sale` (a deal won, a payment that stands) are out.

includeOptedOut.description: Default false: people the CRM marks do-not-contact are out.

allOf.description: A part of the brand's own CRM. Inside a list any one entry matches; across keys all must match. Clients and opted-out people are always out unless stated.
Only people in this part of the brand's own CRM (pipeline stage, tag, funnel step...). Scopes a CRM sourcing to a segment.

people.description: Serve from the brand's merged PEOPLE (one row per human, every source) instead of its CSV rows. Exclusive with uploadIds. Always excludes automated senders, people not about this brand, anyone without an email, and anyone the CRM marks do-not-contact (unless segment.includeOptedOut). Same brand-wide no-re-serve: every address of a served person is suppressed, and a person any address of whom was served before is never served.

reachableBy.description: The channel(s) the pipe serving writes on (all required): `phone` (WhatsApp, calls, SMS) or `email`. On BOTH pools, a contact or person the pipe cannot reach is SKIPPED and NOT marked served, so it stays available to a pipe that can. Omit = no requirement (unchanged behaviour).

relationships.description: The pipe's relationship policy (its lead strategy, forwarded by human-service). `business_only`: lead-service is asked who each candidate is to the brand (POST /internal/brands/{brandId}/relationships/query); nobody tagged personal, investor, supplier, team, partner or advisor (sure or unsure), nobody lead-service never judged, nobody without a human id is handed out, on BOTH pools. Such a person is NOT marked served (another pipe may still write to them). lead-service unreadable = 502 relationships_unavailable, nothing served. Omit = unchanged behaviour.

reached.description: The person reached one of these steps (any source the brand connected).

notReached.description: The person reached none of these steps.

allOf.description: The SERVING PIPE's funnel-step filter (stated by the play's workflow, forwarded by lead-service and human-service), cross-org words only: never a client's stage or tag name. ANDed with the pool and the audience's own filter, on BOTH pools (a CSV row is judged on the person holding its address). Clients are ALWAYS out when it is present. `sale` = a deal won, a payment that stands, or a CRM stage / tag Jev judged `client`; `disqualified` = a CRM stage / tag Jev judged `disqualified` (unqualified, bad fit, blocked: GET /orgs/gohighlevel/label-verdicts).
The serving pipe's funnel-step filter (see StepFilter). A person outside it is skipped and NOT marked served. Omit = unchanged behaviour.

parameters.description: Correlation id for this request. Echoed back verbatim in the `x-request-id` response header. Omit it and the gateway generates a UUID, so the response header is always present. Useful for tying a response back to the call that produced it when issuing concurrent requests.

parameters.name: x-org-id
parameters.description: With a user key (`distrib.usr_*`): the organization this request acts in, one of the key user's organizations (GET /v1/me lists them). Same as the `orgId` query parameter. Needed only when the user belongs to several organizations and the request names no brand; otherwise optional.

parameters.name: x-user-id
parameters.description: External user ID (e.g. Clerk user ID `user_2abc...`). Required when using an app key (`distrib.app_*`) on endpoints that need user context. Ignored when using a user key (`distrib.usr_*`).

parameters.name: x-campaign-id
parameters.description: Campaign ID. Automatically injected by workflow-service on workflow HTTP calls. Optional — forwarded to downstream services for tracking.

parameters.name: x-brand-id
parameters.description: Brand ID(s), comma-separated UUIDs. Supports multi-brand campaigns. Forwarded to downstream services. With a user key it also selects the organization the request acts in: the one of the user's organizations holding every named brand (same for `brandId` in the query or a JSON body).

parameters.name: x-workflow-slug
parameters.description: Workflow slug. Automatically injected by workflow-service on workflow HTTP calls. Optional — forwarded to downstream services for tracking.

parameters.name: x-feature-slug
parameters.description: Feature slug. Optional — forwarded to downstream services and runs for tracking.

post.summary: Start linking a brand's WhatsApp / Telegram / Discord account
post.description:
Proxy to crm-service POST /orgs/matrix/links — starts a bridge login (QR or phone pairing code) the user completes on their phone. Request body forwarded verbatim. Requires x-user-id. Can take up to ~60s (pairing code). Status and body of every refusal are forwarded verbatim: 409 when the channel is not available yet, 422 when the bridge refused (e.g. a bad phone number). Response shape owned by crm-service.

Request body: documented from crm-service POST /orgs/matrix/links, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

method.description: Required to start or relink. Absent when answering `input`.

linkId.description: With `input`: the link whose waiting step is answered. With `method` alone: relink THAT account (expired session, same mirror). Absent: ADD a new account (a fresh flow; linked accounts untouched).

input.description: Answer to the link's waiting step (`link.input`): field id → value. Relayed to the bridge, never stored.

patch.summary: Update a linked account: outreach default, automation allowed, sender persona
patch.description:
Proxy to crm-service PATCH /orgs/matrix/links/{linkId}. Send `brandId` plus at least one of: `outreachDefault: true` (a first WhatsApp message to a person no linked account already talks with goes out from this account; an existing conversation keeps its account; one per brand and channel, the others lose it), `automationAllowed` (whether automated messages may go out from this account), `persona` (the sender persona `{name?, role?, instructions?}`, or null to clear it). Request body forwarded verbatim. Status and body of every refusal are forwarded verbatim. Response shape owned by crm-service.

Proxy to crm-service POST /orgs/stripe/connections. Body (`{ brandId }`) forwarded verbatim. Requires x-user-id: crm-service persists the creator so the sync cron can attribute the org run it opens. post.summary: Connect a brand to Clerk
post.description:
Proxy to crm-service POST /orgs/clerk/connections. Body (`{ brandId }`) forwarded verbatim. Requires x-user-id: crm-service persists the creator so the sync cron can attribute the org run it opens. The connection is written only once the credential has been PROVEN against Clerk, so a credential Clerk refuses comes back 400 carrying `{ type, error, vendorStatus, vendorError }` field-for-field. Response shape owned by crm-service.

Request body: documented from crm-service POST /orgs/clerk/connections, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

post.summary: Merge two people into one person (they are the same human)
post.description:
Merge two people of a brand into ONE person when they are the same person on different channels and no source record says so (a WhatsApp chat with a number nobody saved, and the same human on Gmail or in the CRM). Proxy to crm-service POST /orgs/people/merges. Body `{ brandId, personIds: [personId, personId], reason? }` (the two personId values from GET /v1/orgs/people) forwarded verbatim. The two people become one merged thread with every channel and identity key of both; one person id is kept and the other still opens it. A rebuild starts at once: the merged person shows on GET /v1/orgs/people within about a minute. Idempotent: stating the same two people again answers 200 with `duplicate: true` (201 for a new merge). Refusals cross verbatim with their reason: 404 `person_not_found`, 422 `different_brand` / `same_person`, 409 `already_one_person`. Unmerge with POST /v1/orgs/people/merges/{mergeId}/undo. Requires x-user-id (recorded as who stated it). Response shape owned by crm-service.

Request body: documented from crm-service POST /orgs/people/merges, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

post.summary: Unmerge two people (undo a stated merge)
post.description:
Unmerge: take back a merge stated with POST /v1/orgs/people/merges. Proxy to crm-service POST /orgs/people/merges/{mergeId}/undo, body `{ brandId }` forwarded verbatim. The two people come back apart, each with its own person id, at the rebuild that starts now (unless a source record ties them on its own). The merge stays listed with who undid it and when. Idempotent: undoing twice answers `duplicate: true`. An unknown merge is 404 `merge_not_found`, crm-service's body verbatim. Requires x-user-id. Response shape owned by crm-service.

Request body: documented from crm-service POST /orgs/people/merges/{mergeId}/undo, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

post.summary: Correct a person's tag, company, or an email domain verdict
post.description:
Correct how distribute.you matched a brand's people. Proxy to crm-service POST /orgs/people/corrections, body forwarded verbatim. Kinds: `tag_add` / `tag_remove` `{ brandId, kind, personId, tag }` (one of the four connection tags: personal_to_user, personal_not_to_user, professional_to_brand, professional_not_to_brand); `organization_add` `{ brandId, kind, personId, domain (or website), tags? }` (the person speaks for that company) / `organization_remove` `{ brandId, kind, personId, companyId }`; `domain_kind` `{ brandId, kind, domain, domainKind: mailbox_provider | organization }` (a domain is a public mailbox, or a company). Optional `reason`. Your statement wins over the automatic answer until undone; a newer statement on the same thing replaces the older. A rebuild starts at once (about a minute). Same statement twice answers 200 with `duplicate: true` (201 for a new one). Refusals cross verbatim with their reason: 404 `person_not_found`, 422 `company_unresolved` / `tags_required`. Take it back with POST /v1/orgs/people/corrections/{correctionId}/undo. Requires x-user-id (recorded as who stated it). Response shape owned by crm-service.

Request body: documented from crm-service POST /orgs/people/corrections, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

get.summary: List the companies a brand's people speak for, with their people and tags
get.description: Proxy to crm-service GET /orgs/people/organizations (read-only): one row per company at least one person of the brand speaks for in a work role, most people first, with its people and the professional connection tags they carry (and how many carry each). Read off the last people build. The whole query string is forwarded byte-for-byte (`brandId` required downstream; `limit`, `offset` optional). Requires x-user-id. Response shape owned by crm-service.

post.description: Step 1 of opening a distribute.you account as an AI agent, with no API key and no human. post.summary: Verify the code and get an API key (no API key needed)
post.description: Step 2: send the email and the 6-digit code; get back a working API key plus your org and user ids. A new email opens an account (organization + user; the email is the account's contact, the person can later sign in to the dashboard with it). An email that already has an account gets a NEW additional key for that same account (`created: false`): call start + complete again whenever you need another key. The account has NO free credit: free endpoints work at once, and anything that spends money answers 402 `payment_required` until you prepay (see `prepay` in the answer). A 429 with `error: "too_many_attempts"` means this code is burned after too many wrong tries: request a new one with POST /v1/agent-signups/start (any other 429 is the rate limit). Agent flow, no human needed except to pay: (1) POST /v1/agent-signups/start with your email + phone, (2) read the 6-digit code in that inbox, (3) POST /v1/agent-signups/complete with email + code → `apiKey`, (4) call any free endpoint with `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`, (5) before anything that spends money, POST /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_checkout and have the returned `url` paid. There is no free credit.

post.summary: Prepay: get a payment link (amount you choose, auto top-up required)
post.description: Call this when a call answered 402 `payment_required`, or before anything that spends money. Returns `url`, a hosted card payment page charging `topup_amount_cents`. Paying it credits the balance with exactly that amount (no free credit is ever added), saves the card, and arms the MANDATORY automatic top-up: whenever the balance would fall below `auto_topup_threshold_cents`, the card is charged `auto_topup_amount_cents`. Minimums: $10 prepay, $15 reload, $5 threshold; below a minimum the answer is 400 `amount_below_minimum` naming the `field` and its `minimum_cents` (a missing or non-integer amount is 400 `invalid_amount`). No subscription on this path. You cannot pay the page yourself unless you hold a card: give `url` to your human. Then poll GET /v1/billing/accounts/prepaid_status until `state` is `active`. Example: prepay $10 → balance $10; it drops under $5 → the card is charged $15. Answer from billing-service, verbatim: `{url, session_id, org_id, payment_mode: "prepaid", free_credit_offer, topup_amount_cents, auto_topup: {amount_cents, threshold_cents}}`.

get.summary: Prepaid status: paid yet? balance, auto top-up, can the card be reloaded?
get.description: Read after giving a payment `url` to your human, and whenever a paid call is refused. `state`: `awaiting_payment` (nothing paid yet: the page has not been paid, open a new checkout if the link expired) | `active` (paid, auto top-up armed, card reloadable: you can spend) | `card_not_reloadable` (paid, but the card cannot be charged automatically, `card.not_reloadable_reason` says why: `no_saved_card`, `card_issuing_country_unsupported`, `prepaid_card`, `recurring_charge_not_authorized`, `card_unusable`; the balance is spendable but will not refill: ask your human to pay a new prepaid checkout with another card) | `auto_topup_off` (prepaid without reload: open a prepaid checkout to arm it) | `not_prepaid` (the org pays another way). Also `balance_cents`, `paid_cents`, `auto_topup {enabled, amount_cents, threshold_cents}`, `card {saved, reloadable, not_reloadable_reason}`. Answer from billing-service, verbatim; 404 = no billing account yet (nothing paid).

post.summary: Reply to a person in their existing email thread
post.description:
Send an answer into the email thread a person already has with the brand, from the mailbox and persona that wrote to them (the reply a sales rep would send). Name the person by `email` alone: the thread is found from it. When that person wrote back on several campaigns the answer is 409 `ambiguous_thread` with the `candidates`; call again with one `campaign_id`. Write `body_html` without a signature (the persona's is added). Send `sent_by: "human"` for a reply a person decided on. Name the organization with `brandId` or `orgId`. To send files, list offer documents in `attachments` [{ document_id }] (up to 5, 10 MB together; ids from `GET /v1/brands/{id}/offers/{offerId}/documents`): each goes as a real email attachment, and any problem refuses the whole reply, nothing sent (404 `attachment_not_found`, 422 `attachment_too_large` or `attachments_unsupported_on_transport`, 502 `attachment_unavailable`). Pass-through to instantly-service POST /orgs/replies: refusals come back unchanged with a `code` (409 `ambiguous_thread`, `no_reply_to_thread`, `human_took_over`; 404 `campaign_not_found` when the org never emailed that person). The full body is documented from instantly-service.

Request body: documented from instantly-service POST /orgs/replies, which owns and validates it; the gateway forwards it unchanged.

campaign_id.description: Logical campaign id — the same key manual qualifications and opt-outs use. OPTIONAL: omit it and the thread is found from `email` alone. A thread is a campaign of this org in which the prospect wrote back. Exactly one → the reply goes into it. Several → 409 `ambiguous_thread` listing each candidate (`campaign_id` + `last_message_at`); call again naming one. None but we did email them → 409 `no_reply_to_thread`. Never emailed by this org → 404 `campaign_not_found`. When given, it is used as-is.

email.description: The prospect who replied. Matched case-insensitively. Enough on its own to find the thread when `campaign_id` is omitted.

body_html.description: The answer, HTML. Signed by this service with the sending account's persona — do NOT include a signature.

sent_by.description: Who asked for this answer to be sent. It decides ONE thing: whether the human-takeover gate applies. An `automation` reply is refused (409 `human_took_over`) once a person has answered the thread since the prospect last wrote and that answer is not yet counted as our touch; a `human` reply is never gated. Absent resolves to `automation` — the automated responder is the only caller today, so the gate is live without waiting on it, and a human surface declares `human` explicitly.

document_id.description: An offer document id (UUID) from brand-service, of THIS org (x-org-id).

attachments.description: Offer documents to attach to the reply as real files (a case study, a one-pager). This service reads each one from brand-service, bytes included, as this org, and attaches it under brand-service's filename and type. Up to 5, 10 MB together. FAIL LOUD, nothing sent: unknown or another org's document = 404 `attachment_not_found`; over the limits = 422 `attachment_too_large`; brand-service unreadable = 502 `attachment_unavailable`; a thread on the Instantly pipe (no attachment support) = 422 `attachments_unsupported_on_transport`. Absent or empty = the reply exactly as before. Replies only: cold sequence steps never carry a file.

post.summary: Get a link to connect Telegram for the organization's notices
post.description: Telegram notices: one short line to the organization's owner when one of our workflows acts for the organization (for example, a post was published). Open `linkUrl` (`https://t.me/<bot>?start=<code>`) and press Start in Telegram: that chat then gets the notices. Good once, for 30 minutes (`expiresAt`). Connecting again replaces the chat linked before. No body: the member connecting is taken from the key. Pass-through to client-service POST /internal/orgs/{orgId}/owner-telegram/link-codes.

get.summary: Review who each person is to a brand: unsure merges, unsure tags, unknown companies, and everything settled
get.description: What the brand's relationship review needs: `mergeQuestions` (two people the AI thinks may be the same person, each with a `confidence` and a `reason`), `tagQuestions` (a tag the AI is unsure about), `companyQuestions` (people whose company is unknown, with candidates), `settled` (merges done and every person with their company and tags) and `counts`. Fix each with the POST/PUT/DELETE routes under the same path. Tags: `personal` (about the PERSON, shown on every brand) and `customer`, `prospect`, `team`, `investor`, `advisor`, `supplier`, `partner`, `other_professional` (about this person at this brand). Pass-through to lead-service GET /orgs/brands/{brandId}/relationships/review.

post.summary: Answer a merge question: are these two the same person?
post.description: `{same: true}` links the two people as one person (for this organization only); `{same: false}` records them as different people and the question is never asked again. Undo a merge with POST .../relationships/merges/{linkId}/undo. Pass-through to lead-service POST /orgs/brands/{brandId}/relationships/merge-questions/{questionId}/answer.
